You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

## Diagnosis

The current bug report describes an issue where the CorrelatedRandomVectorGenerator fails silently when faced with zero rows in the covariance matrix. The bug report specifically mentions three matrices that produce different results when sampling a multivariate Gaussian using the generator. These matrices are permutations of each other and have entries with zero values.

Looking at the failing test `testMath789` in `RectangularCholeskyDecompositionTest`, we can see that the test creates three different matrices (`m1`, `m2`, `m3`) using `MatrixUtils.createRealMatrix` and then performs Cholesky decomposition on each matrix. After decomposition, it rebuilds the matrix and asserts that the norm of the difference between the original matrix and the rebuilt matrix is within a certain threshold.

The failing test involves matrices with entries that are permutations of each other and contain zero values. This aligns with the description in the bug report where different results are observed for similar matrices with zero values when using the CorrelatedRandomVectorGenerator.

Therefore, the root cause of the bug is likely related to how the Cholesky decomposition is handled in the presence of zero values in the input matrix, causing discrepancies in the results.

## Next Steps
To address this issue, the handling of zero values in the Cholesky decomposition process needs to be reviewed and potentially improved. Specifically, the code responsible for the Cholesky decomposition in the `RectangularCholeskyDecomposition` class should be inspected and modified to handle zero values appropriately.

## Suggestions for Fixing
- `RectangularCholeskyDecomposition.getRootMatrix()`

Please review and update the Cholesky decomposition implementation to handle zero values correctly to resolve the discrepancy issue observed in the failing test and described in the bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
